text: Light Double Tap: touch the sensor twice without clicking. Finger Match works on the Lock Screen only.
Up, then Down is two quick presses; it runs as the second button goes down. While one is assigned, a single press waits a moment for the other button.
Press the lock button and a volume button together. Holds run after half a second; keep holding and iOS's power-off slider still appears.
Hold is what iOS uses for the button's own action. Assign Hold to replace it; Press and Double Press are extra.
Toggled Twice: flip it and back quickly; it runs on the flip back. While it's assigned, a single flip waits a moment.
Double tap the line at the bottom, inside apps. Single taps still work.
Gestures that start on the big Lock Screen clock. The rest of the Lock Screen is unchanged.
The button on wired headphones. Hold replaces Siri while it's assigned.
Left and Right are each half of the bar. A single tap still scrolls to the top.
A quick flick that starts on an app or folder icon.
Slide from the very edge of the screen. An assigned part of an edge stops doing its iOS gesture there, so open a trigger to see what it takes over.
On an empty part of a Home Screen page, not on an icon.
Inside apps. The app still sees the gesture too, so pick ones it doesn't use; two- and three-finger taps and swipes are safest.
Uses iOS's own shake detection, so no extra battery.
Taking out an AirPod can count as Headphones Disconnected.
Worked out from the location iOS already has. No tracking.
Phone, FaceTime and other calling apps.
Any notification. Triggr only sees which app sent it. For one app, use Custom Events.
Any app in Now Playing: Music, Spotify, YouTube, podcasts…
The sensor by the earpiece. It stays on while the screen is on (a little battery). Wave is a quick cover; with Wave assigned, Cover waits half a second.
Runs after the change. Control Center's Wi-Fi button only leaves the network; Wi-Fi stays on.
The Home Screen will restart. Open apps close.
